label: ex:quantum-universe-su2
title: $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ as a quantum universe
html:
Continuing rigid monoidal Vect, we verify the quantum universe axioms for G = \mathrm{SU}(2).

(i) Category. \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is the category of finite-dimensional complex representations. This is a \mathbb{C}-linear rigid monoidal category. The G-action on tensor products is diagonal; on duals it is the contragredient.

(ii) Frobenius--Hopf object. A = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is the coordinate ring. Its Hopf structure encodes the group operations (see Table 1). The Frobenius pairing is positive definite.

(iii) Fibre functor. \tau \colon \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) \to \mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbb{C}} is the forgetful functor. It is exact, faithful, and monoidal. By Tannaka--Krein duality, G \cong \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau).

(iv) Differential calculus. The left-invariant calculus on \mathrm{SU}(2) provides \Omega^1(A) = \mathrm{span}\{\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3\}. The universal derivation d \colon A \to \Omega^1(A) acts by df = \sum_i (\partial_i f) \omega_i.

(v) Braiding. In \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) the braiding is the flip c_{V,W}(v \otimes w) = w \otimes v, which is symmetric: c_{W,V} \circ c_{V,W} = \mathrm{id}. The first axiom asks for the well-ordering \prec_c that a braiding induces on the Hecke basis, and a symmetric braiding induces none — the ordering is supplied only when c_{V,V}^{2} \neq \mathrm{id}, as the statement on braiding-induced orderings in the next chapter makes precise. So the example at q = 1 verifies axioms 2–4 and is the symmetric point of the family that verifies all four: \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) for q \neq 1, whose braiding on V \otimes V is the R-matrix \check R(q) with eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} on the symmetric and antisymmetric parts, so that \check R satisfies the Hecke relation (\check R - q)(\check R + q^{-1}) = 0 and is not symmetric [kassel1995]. Items (i)–(iv) go through for the family with the same simple objects and the same Clebsch–Gordan rule, the Haar state in place of the Haar measure, and the three-dimensional left-covariant calculus in place of the left-invariant forms; what changes at q \neq 1 is exactly the braiding, and with it the ordering that axiom 1 requires. In the Hecke normalisation \check R(q) is the flip plus a diagonal correction that vanishes at q = 1, which is the sense in which the symmetric example is the limit of the braided ones.
